instructions:
### Rules

- Semantic search is unavailable: `text::semanticSimilarity()` fails with "Embeddings are not enabled for this dataset". Use keyword matching with wildcards.
- Text match is token based. Wildcard every keyword. Never match a multi-word phrase as a single pattern.
- `match` array semantics differ by form: an inline array literal (`title match ["data*", "fetch*"]`) is OR, but a *parameterized* array (`title match $stems`) is AND — every term must match. To OR a parameter list, count the matching terms instead: `count($stems[^.title match @]) > 0`.
- `notes` is Portable Text and cannot be matched directly. Use `pt::text(notes) match ...`.

### Schema notes

- A lesson does not store its parent course. Derive it with a reverse reference: `*[_type == "course" && references(^._id)][0]`.
- `modules` is an array of embedded objects on `course`, not documents. A module holds `lessons`, an ordered array of references to lesson documents.
- Module and lesson numbers ("Module 5", "Lesson 5.1") are not stored. They come from array position. Do not report them — the application derives them.
- `video` documents exist but are an internal lookup, not search results. They are outside this context's `groqFilter` and must never be returned or described to the user. A video moment is only ever surfaced through the lesson that uses that video.
- A lesson joins to its video by URL, not by reference: `*[_type == "video" && url == ^.videoUrl][0]`. One video document serves every lesson that embeds it.
- Timestamps resolve in two stages: match `chapters[].label` first, and fall back to `chunks[].text` only when no chapter matches. Chapter labels are authored and clean; transcript text is the noisier backstop. About 2 in 3 videos have chapters, so the fallback matters.
- Never select a whole `chunks` array. Always filter it and slice it (`[0...2]`) — an unfiltered transcript overflows the context window.

### Query patterns

- Lessons matching any of several stems, ranked by which field matched:
  `*[_type == "lesson" && count($stems[^.title match @ || pt::text(^.notes) match @ || ^.keyPoints[] match @]) > 0]{_id, title, "titleHits": count($stems[^.title match @])} | order(titleHits desc)`
- Video moments for a lesson, chapters first then transcript:
  `*[_type == "lesson" && _id in $ids && defined(videoUrl)]{_id, "video": *[_type == "video" && url == ^.videoUrl][0]{"chapterMoments": chapters[count($stems[^.label match @]) > 0][0...2]{startSeconds, label}, "chunkMoments": chunks[count($stems[^.text match @]) > 0][0...2]{startSeconds, text}}}[defined(video)]`
  Operand order is load-bearing: `count($stems[^.label match @]) > 0` is correct, while `count($stems[@ match ^.label]) > 0` parses fine but silently returns nothing.
- A lesson's course and module title:
  `*[_type == "course" && references(^._id)][0]{title, "moduleTitle": modules[lessons[]._ref match ^.^._id][0].title}`

### Ranking

- Rank by specificity: a lesson whose `title` contains the concept outranks one that only mentions it in `notes`.
- Return every genuinely relevant lesson, up to 40. Do not cap at a handful, and do not pad with weak matches.
- A keyword can match the wrong sense of a word — drop matches that do not actually cover the topic.

### Known limitations

- Only `course` and `lesson` are in scope. Instructors and categories are not search results.
